Notation. mu := V.weight, M_V := V.carrier (the carrier; the letter M is reserved for the gradient bound of the test function, as in the statement), theta := V.mult, spt V := V.support, p_x := V.tangentProj x. T := rotatedPlane q = q(R^n x {0}), P := T.starProjection, Q := I - P; |A|^2 := hsNormSq A, ||A|| operator norm (||A|| <= |A|). For x in R^{n+l} write q^{-1} x = graphPoint(a(x), b(x)), a(x) in R^n, b(x) in R^l; a, b are linear, |a(x)| <= |x| and |b(x)| = dist(x, T) = infDist x T. e_1, ..., e_l is the standard basis of R^l and e'_j := q(graphPoint(0, e_j)) (an orthonormal basis of T^perp). F(x') := q(graphPoint(x', f(x'))), Gamma := F(B^n_{sigma/2}) = q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 (sigma/2)), M_1 := M_V cap Gamma. f^j(x') := (f x') j, grad f^j := gradient (fun y => f y j), Df := fderiv f, |Df|^2 := hsNormSq (Df). B_s := closed ball about 0 (in R^{n+l} or R^n), B°_s the open ball; spheres are L^n-null. c_n := e^{n/2}/2, omega_n := unitBallVolume n.

Facts used. (F2) mu-a.e. point lies in spt V and in M_V; mu(K) < infinity for compact K contained in U; since mu = theta H^n restricted to M_V with theta > 0 on M_V, a subset of M_V is mu-null iff it is H^n-null. (Rad) [Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib Rademacher] f is differentiable at L^n-a.e. x' in B°^n_{sigma/2}; there ||Df(x')|| <= 1 (f is 1-Lipschitz on B^n_{sigma/2}), hence |grad f^j(x')| <= 1 for every j, |Df(x')|^2 = sum_j |grad f^j(x')|^2 <= n, and at such points the gradient of the j-th coordinate is the j-th row of Df. (Area) [Simon Ch. 2, Sect. 3; SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon] F is injective and Lipschitz (|F(x') - F(y')|^2 = |x' - y'|^2 + |f(x') - f(y')|^2 <= 2|x' - y'|^2), and for Borel A contained in B°^n_{sigma/2} and Borel phi >= 0, int_{F(A)} phi dH^n = int_A phi(F(x')) J_F(x') dx' with J_F = det(I + Df^T Df)^{1/2}. Since a o F = id and a is 1-Lipschitz, L^n(A) <= H^n(F(A)) <= 2^{n/2} L^n(A); so F maps L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets and preimages under F of H^n-null subsets of Gamma are L^n-null. (Jac) For an l x n matrix D with ||D|| <= 1 and singular values s_i in [0, 1]: |D|^2 = sum s_i^2 <= n, J(D) := det(I + D^T D)^{1/2} = prod (1 + s_i^2)^{1/2} is in [1, 2^{n/2}], and J(D) <= exp(|D|^2/2) <= 1 + c_n |D|^2 (as e^t <= 1 + t e^t for t >= 0 and |D|^2/2 <= n/2). (Proj) For every x, p_x is either an orthogonal projection or 0; in both cases p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent, so (p_x u) . (p_x w) = u . p_x w, |p_x u| <= |u| and ||I - p_x|| <= 1.

Proof. Let C_7 := l + 1/2 + n K_b and C := max{C_7, 2 K_b + 1 + c_n C_7, (1 + c_n n)(omega_n C_7)^{1/2}, 1}; C depends only on n, l, K_b.

1. Localization. (a) If x in spt V cap B_sigma(0) and |a(x)| < sigma/4, then |x| <= |a(x)| + |b(x)| < sigma/4 + sigma/16 = 5 sigma/16 by the height hypothesis. (b) For x' in B^n_{3 sigma/8}, |F(x')|^2 = |x'|^2 + |f(x')|^2 <= (3 sigma/8)^2 + (sigma/16)^2 < (sigma/2)^2, so F(B^n_{3 sigma/8}) is contained in B°_{sigma/2}(0). Fix h_c in C^infinity_c(R^{n+l}; [0, 1]) with h_c = 1 on B_{3 sigma/8}(0) and tsupport h_c contained in B°_{sigma/2}(0).

2. First-variation identity (book (6)). Let zeta, M and j be as in the second conclusion. zeta~ := zeta o a is C^1, grad zeta~(x) = q(graphPoint(grad zeta(a(x)), 0)) lies in T and |grad zeta~| <= M. X := h_c zeta~ e'_j is C^1 with compact support and tsupport X contained in B°_{sigma/2}(0), which is contained in B_sigma(0), contained in U; so X is admissible. If |x| >= sigma/2 then X vanishes near x. Let x in spt V cap B_{sigma/2}(0). If a(x) is not in tsupport zeta, then zeta~ = 0 near x, so X = 0 near x and div_M X(x) = 0 = (p_x e'_j) . (p_x grad zeta~(x)), X(x) = 0 = zeta~(x) e'_j. If a(x) is in tsupport zeta (contained in B°_{sigma/4}), then |x| < 5 sigma/16 by 1(a), so h_c = 1 near x, X = zeta~ e'_j near x, DX(x) v = (grad zeta~(x) . v) e'_j and div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x) = grad zeta~(x) . p_x e'_j = (p_x e'_j) . (p_x grad zeta~(x)) by (Proj), and X(x) = zeta~(x) e'_j. Since mu-a.e. x lies in spt V, the definition of generalized mean curvature gives

and the integrand on the left vanishes for mu-a.e. x outside B_{5 sigma/16}(0). All integrands are mu-measurable (x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis), bounded apart from H (integrable on B_sigma(0)), and supported in B_{sigma/2}(0), of finite measure.

3. Graph part (book (7)). For x' in B°^n_{sigma/2} at which f is differentiable, let P_{x'} := span{q(graphPoint(v, Df(x') v)) : v in R^n} and g_j(F(x')) := q(graphPoint(grad f^j(x'), 0)), an element of T with |g_j| <= 1 and sum_j |g_j(F(x'))|^2 = |Df(x')|^2. The vector e'_j - g_j(F(x')) = q(graphPoint(-grad f^j(x'), e_j)) is orthogonal to P_{x'}, because <graphPoint(-grad f^j(x'), e_j), graphPoint(v, Df(x') v)> = -grad f^j(x') . v + (Df(x') v)_j = 0. Hence p_x e'_j = p_x g_j(x) whenever p_x = P_{a(x)}.starProjection. By the tangent-plane hypothesis this holds for mu-a.e. x in M_1 with a(x) in B°^n_{sigma/2} and f differentiable at a(x); the remaining points of Gamma are F(Z) with Z the L^n-null set of x' in B^n_{sigma/2} with |x'| = sigma/2 or f not differentiable at x', and H^n(F(Z)) <= 2^{n/2} L^n(Z) = 0, so mu(F(Z)) = 0. Thus, for mu-a.e. x in M_1, p_x e'_j = p_x g_j(x) and p_x is the orthogonal projection onto the n-dimensional subspace P_{a(x)} (set g_j := 0 at the exceptional points).

(p_x grad zeta~) dmu| <= M mu(B_{sigma/2}(0) cap (spt V \ Gamma)) <= M K_b E sigma^n, by the bad-set hypothesis (its first summand).
